spots.name: Lalbagh Fort

hours.note: Closed Sat

spots.summary: The Lalbagh Fort is a historic fort situated in the old city of Dhaka, Bangladesh. Its name is derived from its neighbourhood, Lalbagh, which means Red Garden. The term Lalbagh refers to reddish and pinkish hues in the Mughal architecture. The original fort was called Fort Aurangabad.

names.ja: ラールバーグ・フォート

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Shmunmun assumed (based on copyright claims

spots.name: Ahsan Manzil
spots.summary: Ahsan Manzil is a historic palace situated in Kumartoli along the banks of Buriganga River in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It served as the official residence and administrative seat of the Nawab of Dhaka during the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

names.ja: アシャーン・マンズィル

spots.name: Baitul Mukarram

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Baitul Mukarram, officially Baitul Mukarram National Mosque, is the national mosque of Bangladesh. It is located at the center of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. The mosque was completed in 1968. It has a capacity of more than 42,000 worshippers.

names.ja: バイトゥル・ムカッラム

spots.name: Dhakeshwari Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dhakeshwari National Temple is a Hindu temple in Old Dhaka, Bangladesh. It is state-owned, giving it the distinction of being Bangladesh's 'National Temple'. The name "Dhakeshwari" means "Goddess of Dhaka". Dhaka is named after Goddess Dhakeshwari.

names.ja: ダケーシュワリー寺院

spots.name: Shaheed Minar
spots.summary: The Shaheed Minar is a national monument in Dhaka, Bangladesh, established to commemorate those killed during the Bengali language movement demonstrations of 1952 in then East Pakistan.

spots.name: Old Dhaka
spots.summary: Old Dhaka is a term used to refer to the historic old city of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. Located on the banks of the Buriganga River, it was one of the largest and most prosperous cities of the Indian subcontinent, and the center of the worldwide muslin trade.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Three Leaders
spots.summary: The Mausoleum of Three Leaders, officially Three National Leaders' Shrine, located at Shahbag, New Dhaka in Bangladesh. It contains the graves of three prominent leaders of Pakistan Movement from Bengal: A. K. Fazlul Huq, Huseyn Shaheed Suhrawardy and Khwaja Nazimuddin.

spots.name: Star Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Star Mosque is a mosque located in Armanitola area, Dhaka, Bangladesh. The mosque has ornate designs and is decorated with motifs of blue stars. It was built in the first half of the 19th century by Mirza Golam Pir. It is also the image on the ৳100 note on the Bangladeshi taka currency.

spots.name: Bangladesh National Museum
spots.summary: The Bangladesh National Museum is the national repository of Bangladesh's cultural and historical artifacts, located in the Shahbag area of Dhaka.

names.ja: バングラデシュ国立博物館

spots.name: Bangabandhu Memorial Museum

hours.note: Closed Wed

spots.summary: Bangabandhu Memorial Museum, also known as Bangabandhu Bhaban or Dhanmondi 32, was a museum located in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, Bangladesh, which was once the personal residence of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding president of Bangladesh.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Ziaur Rahman
spots.summary: The Mausoleum Complex of Ziaur Rahman is a significant architectural engineering monument located in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar of Dhaka city in Bangladesh. The monument hosts the grave of Ziaur Rahman, president of Bangladesh from 1977 to 1981.

spots.name: Anti Terrorism Raju Memorial Sculpture
spots.summary: Anti Terrorism Raju Memorial Sculpture is a sculpture located in University of Dhaka campus of Bangladesh.

spots.name: Armenian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Armenian Church, also known as Armenian Apostolic Church of the Holy Resurrection, is a historically significant architectural monument situated in the Armanitola area of old Dhaka, Bangladesh.

names.fr: Église de la Sainte-Résurrection de Dhaka

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Mak assumed (based on copyright claims).

spots.name: Mausoleum of Kazi Nazrul Islam
spots.summary: The mausoleum of Kazi Nazrul Islam is a mausoleum located in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. It marks the grave of Kazi Nazrul Islam, the 20th-century writer, musician, and the national poet of Bangladesh. He died on 29 August 1976 and was buried here in the same year. Later, his grave was converted into a mausoleum.

spots.name: Gurdwara Nanak Shahi

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gurdwara Nanak Shahi is the principal Sikh gurdwara (temple), located in Nilkhet, Dhaka, Bangladesh. It is located at the campus of the University of Dhaka and considered to be the biggest of the 9 to 10 gurdwaras in the country. The gurdwara commemorates the visit of Guru Nanak (1506–1507).

spots.name: Mughal Eidgah

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dhanmondi Shahi Eidgah, also known as Mughal Eidgah, is located in Saat Masjid road, in Dhanmondi residential area of Dhaka, Bangladesh. The Eidgah was built in 1640 CE during the Mughal era and has been in use for Eid celebration since then.

spots.name: Bangladesh Military Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bangladesh Military Museum is a military museum in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Administered by the Bangladesh Army, the museum is located next to the Novo Theatre at Bijoy Sarani of the capital Dhaka.

names.zh: 孟加拉國防軍事博物館

spots.name: Liberation War Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Liberation War Museum is a museum at Agargaon in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, which commemorates the Bangladesh Liberation War that led to the independence of Bangladesh from Pakistan.

names.es: Museo de la Guerra de Liberación

spots.name: Shahbaz Khan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shahbaz Khan Mosque is a historic Sunni Hanafi mosque, located in Dhaka, in the Dhaka District of Bangladesh. Situated near Mir Jumla’s Gate, the mosque serves as an example of late Mughal architecture in Bengal, known as the Shaista Khan architectural style.

spots.name: Museum of Independence

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Museum of Independence in Dhaka, Bangladesh depicts the struggle for independence of Bangladesh. It shows the history of the nation since Mughal tenure to independence in 1971. It is the first and only underground museum in the country.

spots.name: Musa Khan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Musa Khan Mosque is a Sunni mosque, located in the southern part of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Muntasir du assumed (based on copyright cla

spots.name: Aparajeyo Bangla
spots.summary: Aparajeyo Bangla is one of the most well known sculptures dedicated to the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971. It is located in the campus of the University of Dhaka, just in front of the Faculty of Arts Building. In Bengali, the phrase means "Unvanquished Bengal".

spots.name: Ramna Kali Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Ramna Kali Temple is a Hindu temple in Dhaka, Bangladesh, that was originally built during the Mughal Empire. It was also known as the "Ramna Kalibari". The temple is dedicated to the Hindu Goddess Kali.

names.ja: ラムナ・カリ・マンディール

spots.name: Hussaini Dalan
spots.summary: The Hussaini Dalan is a Twelver Shi'ite Imambara that was originally built during the later half of the Mughal rule in the 17th century in Dhaka. It was built as the Imambara of the Shia Muslim community.

spots.name: Zia Udyan
spots.summary: Zia Udyan or Zia Uddan, also known as Chandrima Uddan is a park situated across the National Parliament Building in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

spots.name: Ramna Park
spots.summary: Ramna Park is an urban green space renowned for its historical significance and recreational amenities, situated at the centre of Dhaka, Bangladesh.

spots.name: Saat Masjid

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sat Gambuj Mosque is a Sunni mosque and tomb complex located near the northwestern outskirts of Dhaka in the Mohammadpur area, in the Dhaka District of Bangladesh. The mosque is a fine example of the provincial Mughal-style architecture introduced in the 17th century in what is now Bangladesh.

spots.name: Baldha Garden
spots.summary: Baldha Garden is a botanical garden which spans 3.15 acres (1.27 ha) of land located at Wari in the old part of the city of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. It has a collection of 672 species of plants. The Baldha Garden is now managed as a satellite unit of the National Botanical Garden by the Department of Forestry.

spots.name: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman statue destruction
spots.summary: On 5 August 2024, after the resignation of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina following the July Uprising, a large golden statue of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the first president of Bangladesh and Hasina's father, at the Mrityunjayee Prangan in Bijoy Sarani, Dhaka was destroyed by the protesters.

spots.name: Banani graveyard
spots.summary: The Banani graveyard is a cemetery in the Banani neighbourhood of Dhaka. It is one of eight state-run graveyards in Dhaka and, with a capacity for around 22,000 graves, one of the largest graveyards in that city. It covers approximately 10 acres and two to three burials take place every day.

spots.name: Greek Memorial, Dhaka
spots.summary: Greeks were the last among European merchants to come to Bangladesh. They came to Bangladesh around the 18th century. They constructed a memorial in Dhaka. It was constructed for the memory of the Greek merchants who died while in Dhaka.

spots.name: Bangladesh Air Force Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Bangladesh Air Force Museum is the first aviation museum in Bangladesh, located in Agargaon, Dhaka. This museum was established in 1987 with the aim of preserving the history, achievements, and progress of the Bangladesh Air Force and presenting them.

spots.name: City Centre Dhaka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: City Centre Dhaka is a commercial high-rise building located in Motijheel, Dhaka, and is the second tallest building in Bangladesh. It is located at the heart of Motijheel, It rises up to a height of 118 m (387 ft).

spots.name: Shapla Square
spots.summary: Shapla Square is an iconic landmark and sculpture at the heart of Motijheel, a central business district, near the center of Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. It depicts a Shapla or water lily, the national flower of Bangladesh.

spots.name: Dhanmondi Lake
spots.summary: Dhanmondi Lake, located in the middle of Dhaka, Bangladesh, is a prominent urban water body known for its picturesque setting and recreational opportunities.

spots.name: Binat Bibi Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Binat Bibi Mosque is the earliest surviving mosque in Dhaka, built in 1454 by Bakht Binat, the daughter of Marhamat. It was built during the rule of the Sultan of Bengal, Nasiruddin Mahmud Shah (1435–1459). The mosque is located beside the Hayat Bepari's Bridge in the Narinda area.

photo.author: No machine-readable author provided. Mak assumed (based on copyright claims).

spots.name: SAARC Fountain
spots.summary: SAARC Fountain is a fountain in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It is situated at Kawran Bazar, at the intersection of Panthapath, Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and Sonargaon Road, and is adjacent to the Pan Pacific Sonargaon hotel.

spots.name: Tagore sculpture controversy
spots.summary: Tagore Sculpture Controversy was an incident in the campus area of Dhaka University, Bangladesh. On 14 February 2023, a temporary sculpture of Rabindranath Tagore was installed there by some student to make people aware of various issues in the country.

spots.name: Khan Mohammad Mridha Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Khan Mohammad Mridha Mosque is a historical mosque near Lalbagh Fort in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

spots.name: National Museum of Science and Technology

hours.note: Closed Thu

spots.summary: The National Museum of Science and Technology (NMST) in Dhaka, Bangladesh was founded on April 26, 1965, by the Pakistani government and became a part of Bangladesh's Ministry of Science and Technology following the Bangladesh Liberation War.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Science and Technology (Bangladesh)

names.de: Nationales Museum für Wissenschaft und Technologie (Bangladesch)

spots.name: Gulshan Society Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gulshan Society Mosque, also called Gulshan Society Jame Masjid, is a mosque in Gulshan, a neighbourhood in Dhaka. It was planned by Kashef Chowdhury and completed in 2017 for Gulshan Society.

spots.name: Dhaka University Library

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: The Dhaka University Library is the central library of the University of Dhaka, Bangladesh, which started in 1921 with a collection of 18,000 books received from Dhaka College and Law College. The Library now has over 680,000 books and journals. Moreover, it has around 30,000 rare manuscripts.

names.es: Biblioteca de la Universidad de Daca

spots.name: Bahadur Shah Park
spots.summary: Bahadur Shah Park, formerly Victoria Park, is a historically significant urban park located in Old Dhaka, Bangladesh. Developed in the 19th century, it commemorates the soldiers who died during the Indian Rebellion of 1857 against British colonial rule.

spots.name: National Stadium, Dhaka
spots.summary: National Stadium, Dhaka is a multipurpose sports arena and the national stadium of Bangladesh. Located in the Motijheel area of Dhaka, it is predominantly used for football matches and serves as the home venue for the Bangladesh national football team.

names.ja: バンガバンドゥ・ナショナル・スタジアム

spots.name: Moder Gorob
spots.summary: Moder Gorob is a sculpture situated in front of Bangla Academy building in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It was dedicated to the memory of those killed during the Bengali language movement demonstrations of 1952, when protesters demanding Bengali as a state language of former Dominion of Pakistan were massacred by Pakistan Police.

spots.name: Nimtali arch
spots.summary: The Nimtali arch is an arch in Dhaka, Bangladesh dating from the Mughal period. It was the gateway to the palace of the Naib Nazim of Dhaka, the deputy governor of Bengal Subah in the Mughal Empire.

spots.name: National Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Art Gallery is a fine arts gallery of Shilpakala Academy in Segunbagicha, Dhaka, Bangladesh. It contains works of art from national artists, such as Zainul Abedin and Quamrul Hassan.

spots.name: Navana Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Navana Tower is a high-rise located in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It is located in Gulshan, one of the central business districts of the metropolis. It rises up to a height of 74.07 m (243 ft) and has 23 floors. Navana Tower is the nineteenth tallest high-rise in Dhaka.

spots.name: Kartalab Khan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Kartalab Khan Mosque, also known as the Begum Bazar Mosque, is a mosque, located in the Begum Bazar area in the Old City of Dhaka, Bangladesh. It was built by Nawab Diwan Murshid Quli Khan between 1700 and 1704 CE.

spots.name: Christian Cemetery, Dhaka
spots.summary: The Dhaka Christian Cemetery is a graveyard situated in Wari, an area of the old town in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It was established by Portuguese traders in the 17th century and is still in use by members of the Dhaka Christian community.

spots.name: St Thomas Church, Dhaka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Thomas Cathedral Church is a cathedral belonging to the Diocese of Dhaka of the Church of Bangladesh, which is a United Protestant denomination that formed as a result of a merger between the Anglican and Presbyterian churches in the region. It is the seat of the diocese.

spots.name: National Library of Bangladesh

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Library of Bangladesh is the legal depository of all new books and other printed materials published in Bangladesh under the copyright law of Bangladesh. It was founded in 1973, but it traces its origins back to 1967, before the Bangladesh Liberation War and its independence.

names.ja: バングラデシュ国立図書館

spots.name: Toshakhana

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Toshakhana is a specialized treasury for gifts received by the President and Prime Minister of Bangladesh. The gifts are considered property of the state and are stored in Toshakhana which is part of the Presidential palace, Bangabhaban.

spots.name: St. Mary's Cathedral, Dhaka

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Mary's Cathedral also called Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception is a religious building belonging to the Catholic Church and located in the Kakrail, Ramna, in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It was established in 1956 and his feast is celebrated on December 8.

names.ru: Собор Непорочного Зачатия Пресвятой Девы Марии

spots.name: Swami Bagh Temple

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Swamibagh Temple is a prominent Hindu temple of the Vaishnav culture in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh. There are many temples and an ashram managed by ISKCON, of which Swamibagh temple in Bangladesh is prominent.

spots.name: Rajosik Bihar
spots.summary: Rajosik Bihar is a sculpture of a horse-drawn carriage made by Mrinal Haque. It is situated in front of the Sheraton Hotel at the junction of Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue and Minto Road in Dhaka city's Paribagh. It was erected on the theme of the regal tour of Dhaka city with the families of Nawabs and Zamindars.

spots.name: Central Public Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Sufia Kamal National Public Library is the largest public library in Bangladesh and houses the central administration of the Department of Public Libraries, under the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. The library was named "Central Public Library" between 2004 and 2010.

spots.name: Zero Point
spots.summary: Noor Hossain Square, commonly known as Zero Point, is a square situated in Gulistan, Dhaka, Bangladesh.

spots.name: Doreen Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Doreen Tower is a high-rise skyscraper centered in the Gulshan-2 circle of Dhaka. The 25-story building has a height of 112 meters, and is the 11th tallest building in Bangladesh. It comprises the luxury hotel Four Points by Sheraton.

spots.name: Sena Kalyan Bhaban

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Sena Kalyan Bhaban is a 21-storied commercial building located at 195, Motijheel Commercial Area, Dhaka on an area of 1.35 bighas of land. Previously, on the same space there was a rest house for ex-armed forces personnel. The foundation stone of the 21-storied Sena Kalyan Bhaban was laid in April 1982.

spots.name: Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban
spots.summary: Designed by the famous American architect, Louis I. Kahn, it is renowned as a modern architectural wonder of the region. The Parliament is surrounded by gardens that form a peaceful getaway from the chaos of the city. The building is also surrounded by heavy security. Foreigners have to fill out a form and provide passport photocopies to visit the building. No cameras or phones allowed inside.

spots.name: Institute of Arts and Crafts
spots.summary: Houses a representative collection of folk-art, modern art and paintings by numerous artists of Bangladesh.

spots.name: Curzon Hall
spots.summary: An architecturally beautiful building named after Lord Curzon. Once intended as a town hall, it now houses the Science Faculty of the University of Dhaka.

photo.author: Sajid Muhaimin Choudhury (Transfered by Boles Shikmim/Original uploaded by Smcbu

spots.name: Suhrawardi Udyan
spots.summary: A race course of the British times, it has been converted into a park. It was the place where independence leader Sheikh Mujibur Raman delivered a historic oath of independence speech before the 1971 War, and where the Pakistani army surrendered a few months later. The Shadhinota Stambha monument, a 50-m-high tower of light composed of stacked glass panel, has been erected here. The Museum of Inde

names.zh: 蘇哈拉瓦迪·烏迪安公園

photo.author: Official photographer of the Dhaka Nawab Family

spots.name: Eternal Flame (শিখা চিরন্তন)
spots.summary: The eternal flame was inaugurated by Prime Minister Sheik Hasina on 7 Mrach 1997. The flame burns eternally at the Northern end of Suhrawardi Uddyan, beneath the Bangladesh National flag.

spots.name: Old High Court Building
spots.summary: It was built as the residence of the British Governor, it illustrates a happy blend of European and Mughal architecture. Now houses the Supreme Court.

spots.name: CoFi 11 Express

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Offers different coffee specialities made from imported beans as well as exotic drinks like Lemogini, Shikanjee, Guava Frappe, Mango Yogurt & Mandolito. CoFi 11 has a beautiful terrace with nice view over Gulshan. They also have brownies, waffles, local dishes, and sandwiches. Free WiFi is also available as well as live musical performances from time to time. They also have a branch in Chittagong,

spots.name: Hotel Al-Razzaque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: On the ground floor of the hotel is a large and popular restaurant, busy anytime of the day with Bangladeshi families and businessmen. Food is pretty darn good, if unpredictable in its timing. Sometimes you'll have a choice of chicken and mutton curries, fish and vegetables, other times it's chicken biryani or the highway. Fish will double the price of a meal, at least. It is located between a cle

spots.name: Hajjee Beryani

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Old Dhaka was famed for its lines of biryani restaurants. Some of the more famous outfits are still going and Hajjee Beryani is one of them. It revels in its eccentric reputation for opening only at certain times and only cooking a certain amount (well-below demand).

spots.name: Sura

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Korean restaurant near the Egyptian embassy. Table-top barbecue and most popular Korean dishes are available, along with a selection of sushi and sashimi. Popular with Koreans and other expats. Expect to pay at least Tk 500 per person for a 3-course dinner.

spots.name: North End Coffee

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Definitely the best coffee in Dhaka. With foreign ownership, an on-site coffee-roasting machine and huge sacks of coffee in the back, this is definitely the place to get your caffeine fix. Prices reasonable. No meals yet, just muffins and brownies.

spots.name: A&W

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A burger, fries and rootbeer float will cost nearly BDT300, which seems to be no problem for the well-off young Bangladeshi teens that fill the tables. The jukebox filled with Backstreet Boys may either add or detract from the experience.

spots.name: American Club

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Restaurant, swimming pool, and tennis courts. Although it was built primarily for the employees of the U.S. Embassy in Dhaka and their families, membership is generally available to other people as well.

spots.name: Bashudhara City Food Court

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A large food court in the Bashundhara City Mall with all manner of fast food, western food, Bangladeshi food and more. There is also a slightly higher end Food Hall in the food court.

spots.name: Bamboo Shoot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A Chinese/Thai restaurant that prides itself in offering 'authentic' cuisine, and this is backed up by the number of Chinese expats seen eating there on any given night.

spots.name: Bittersweet Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Famous for the cupcakes, the milk shakes, the cheesecake and other pastries. A wide range of sandwiches and other dishes are also available. Free WLAN is also available.

spots.name: New Café Jheel

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Serves good local dishes for the budget traveler. Expect to pay Tk 150-200 for a 3 course meal. Although you can possibly get lunch/dinner for as low as Tk 60.

spots.name: H. Kabir and Company, Ltd.

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat

spots.summary: is a duty-free shop that is only permitted to sell alcohol to passport-bearing foreigners or their drivers who bring their passports in when they purchase.

spots.name: Jharna Grill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The top restaurant in the hotel serves very good seafood. Expect to pay Tk 3,000 for a 3-course meal with drinks. The hotel has other good restaurants too.

spots.name: Aqua Deck

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A lounge next to the pool in the InterContinental Hotel with things like sandwiches and salads. More affordable than the other restaurants in the hotel.

spots.name: Voot

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An upscale restaurant with a haunted theme (VOOT-meaning ghost in Bengali), high quality food, next to the well known Rifles Square Market.

spots.name: La Diplomat

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Don't expect to be rubbing shoulders with any French ambassadors, however.
